_doc: Guardrails for the idea pipeline: make things people use and pay for with near-zero owner overhead and little financial risk (ownerBudget). Read by bin/idea-pipeline.js. See README.

ownerBudget._why: David, 2026-10-12: "I am ok moving a product forward for a few hundred." Agents still never spend or hold a card (maxMonthlySpendUsd stays 0): they propose a spend with what it should buy (ads to fill a demand test, a domain, a paid tier for a product that takes payments) and David approves and pays.

hosting: Vercel Pro (David upgraded the team on 2026-10-13, which allows commercial use), Neon free. Since 2026-10-31 the Vercel team is soft-blocked until 2026-11-30 (402 on every new deploy and on several products): Cloudflare Workers (free plan, agent account, no card) is the second host. A Next.js product gets the OpenNext adapter (@opennextjs/cloudflare, wrangler.jsonc named after the repo, `npm run cf:build`) and deploys with `provision cloudflare deploy <repo> <checkout>` (ai-stack README, Hosting on Cloudflare Workers); tiebreak runs there. Keep products light enough for both free tiers (Worker bundle under 3 MiB gzip) and ask before anything metered.

seeded._why: Ideas David sends are researched and reviewed on the next pipeline tick, not at 09:00, and the verdict goes back where he sent them (lib/seeds.js). Claude Pro only, shared with his own sessions and M1 builds, so at most maxPerDay runs a day; a failed run (e.g. usage limit) waits retryMinutes; nothing starts in the quiet window around the 09:00 research run. Over the cap, seeds wait for the next day. maxPerDay was 3 until 2026-10-12, when David asked for a batch of ten to be pushed through the same night; research hadn't hit the usage limit in the week before. Runs go one per tick, so ten take about 2.5 hours.

discovery._why: David, 2026-10-12: two dozen researched ideas and nobody had seen the products yet. While new builds wait for a focus product's traction (build.startNew), the 09:00 run records no new idea (bin/idea-research.js discoveryPaused); ideas he sends are still researched. Lifts by itself with the build hold.

build._model: Builds run Claude Code with --model opus --effort xhigh on the subscription. If Opus is overloaded or not available on the plan right now, Claude Code itself drops to claudeFallbackModel (still the subscription, $0). Only when the subscription can't take the work at all does the build move to the free pool (fallback). No local model: the 16 GB Mac can't run a coder strong enough for a milestone.
build._sandbox: "docker": Claude Code, npm install and npm test run in RepoHQ's factory sandbox (no mounts, no host environment or credentials; network only to package registries and api.anthropic.com), logged in with a `claude setup-token` subscription token kept in the keychain under tokenService. The host clones, applies the patch, runs the secret scan and the credential broker, commits and opens the PR. "host": the old way, on the Mac; code the builder writes can read the Mac's files there, so use it only when the sandbox is down and a build can't wait. No token or no Docker in "docker" mode fails the build with the reason; it never falls back to the host.
build._why: Coding a product from its PRD wants the strongest model: Claude Code on the subscription first; the free pool (LiteLLM free-agent) only when the subscription is out of capacity.
build._advisor: RepoHQ tier advisor rates each milestone 1-3 (local model). "report": recorded only, Claude first. "act": a milestone rated 1 starts on the free pool and moves up to Claude on failure. Switch when its score on the factory ladder earns it.
build._concurrency: David's call on 2026-10-13: "push the system to almost its limits", no daily or weekly cap on builds, only how many run at once, "so we don't break the computer". Builds run in their own processes (bin/idea-build-job.js, lib/build-slots.js). At most max at once; each starts only while Docker has reserveMemoryMb to spare, counting every running sandbox at least that much (Docker Desktop's VM is about 5.8 GB, and each sandbox may use up to 4 GB), and the Mac has at least minFreeMemoryPct of its memory free (memory_pressure). On today's Docker allowance that is two builds at once; a third starts when Docker has room for it. Builds the pipeline starts by itself (go-lives, first builds, the rest of a started MVP, growth builds) leave reserveForRequests slots for "Start build now", and one whose last build failed or whose PR was closed waits retryAfterHours (the daily caps used to stop a failing build from looping). A build still running after hungAfterHours is stopped. Every build shares the Claude subscription with David's own sessions: running three at once uses a usage window faster, and builds fall back as before (claudeFallbackModel, then the free pool).
build._mode: "mvp" ("let it rip"): approving a build, and the weekly slot, build every remaining roadmap milestone in one sandbox session, then open one PR. It stops at the first milestone whose tests fail, that falls back off the subscription (stopOnFallback), or after maxMinutes; the PR has what is done and the next build starts there. "milestone": one milestone per build, as before. Start build now offers both.
build._startNew: false: an idea that has never been built waits for its first build (the weekly slot and approvals) until a focus product (growth.focus) has growth.minVisitorsPerWeek unique visitors in 7 days (lib/pipeline.js newBuildsHeld). Ideas already being built carry on, and Start build now still works. David's call on 2026-10-12: distribution before more MVPs. Go-live and growth builds don't count toward maxPerWeek; each has its own cap.

growth._burst: Visits are left out of every count (funnels, experiment windows, demand tests) when burstMinVisitors or more different visitors arrive in one hour with no referrer and never do anything else: a crawler sweep or a test run, not demand (2026-10-15: botchelor.com's 31 visitors within two hours of going live). The hours burstExemptHours after a logged launch post still count, since Reddit's app and many mobile clients send no referrer. The funnel records how many were left out (burst7d). 0 turns it off.
growth._why: The growth loop (RepoHQ docs/growth-loop-prd.md, idea-pipeline step 5d, lib/growth.js). focus: the live products that get a daily growth step, most important first. Each day, the first matching rule picks one mission per product: a growth build (a draft PR, one change), a launch kit (posts David publishes) or an item in the morning email's Today block. At most maxMissionsPerDay missions a day, one per product, maxBuildsPerWeek rule-based growth builds a week (features from the weekly plan count separately: feature.maxPerDay), each in its policy.schedule window, never on a tick that built; nothing new on a product while something waits for David (an open growth PR, an unposted kit). Growth runs use model at effort on the subscription and never fall back to the free pool. auto false stops new missions. minVisitorsPerWeek is the traction bar, which also lifts build.startNew's hold.

plan._why: The weekly plan (lib/plan.js, bin/idea-plan.js; David's call on 2026-10-19). At night, once a week per focus product (sooner once everything in it is built), Claude on the subscription reads the product's record, funnel, experiments and lessons and writes PLAN.md: up to `items` features, each with the metric it should move and acceptance criteria a test can check. Only for products past launch and instrumenting. auto false stops new plans.

feature._why: Feature builds from the weekly plan: one per product at a time, on Opus at xhigh (Claude Code drops to fallbackModel on the subscription if Opus is unavailable; never the free pool). Each is checked against its acceptance criteria by a separate run (one fix round), smoke-tested on its Vercel preview against production before it merges itself, and judged as an experiment when its window ends. Payment code waits for David (autonomy.ownerOnlyPatterns). maxPerDay across products; policy.schedule decides when.

autonomy._why: David's call on 2026-10-12: agents merge everything and he reviews what was done each morning (RepoHQ docs/growth-loop-prd.md, "Autonomy"). merge: the pipeline merges its own PRs (growth, go-live, milestones) once its tests passed and every GitHub check is green (CI, GitGuardian, the Vercel preview), with no conflicts (lib/autonomy.js). A growth PR that fails is closed and its mission tried again the next day; a failed roadmap build waits for David. revert: an agent's merge that breaks the live site's launch checks within a day, or an experiment the judge finds clearly worse, is reverted by a revert PR the pipeline merges, and Slack is told. protectedPaths: PRs touching these (the CI that gates merging) are left for David. Set merge false to go back to David merging everything.
autonomy._ownerOnly: Files a feature PR (the weekly plan's) may not merge itself with: payment code. Matched case-insensitively against each changed path; such a PR waits for David, as does a plan item marked payments. Go-lives and milestone builds aren't affected (a go-live adds the payment link by design).

_signalUrl: The public demand-signal endpoint: landing pages and every product beacon POST here. Since 2026-10-31 the idea-factory Worker (worker/ideas.mjs) on Cloudflare, writing to RepoHQ's idea_signals; RepoHQ's own /api/ideas/signal does the same but RepoHQ now runs on the Mac behind Tailscale, which the public can't reach. Changing it re-renders the live landing pages on the next tick (lib/pipeline.js pageStale); products carry it in their code.
_repohqUrl: Where links to RepoHQ (the Ideas page) point in Slack messages and the seed digest. Since 2026-10-31 RepoHQ runs on David's Mac (ai-stack bin/repohq-web) and his devices reach it over Tailscale; repohq.vercel.app answers 402 until Vercel's block lifts.
_workersSubdomain: The Cloudflare account's workers.dev subdomain: a product deployed as a Worker lives at https://<repo>.<this>.workers.dev. The live check and the production-URL lookup try it next to Vercel, and prefer whichever answers (lib/golive.js pickProduction).
_pagesHost: Where pages/ is published: cloudflare (the idea-factory Worker, provision cloudflare deploy idea-factory <checkout>) or vercel (pagesProject in vercelScope, the old host; 402 since 2026-10-31).

revenue._why: Once an idea's M1 is merged, bin/idea-revenue.js writes its road-to-revenue plan (REVENUE.md, revenue.json) on the Claude subscription: who pays, the price, what must exist before charging, where to launch. The pipeline turns it into the launch checklist (state.launch) and ranks build queues by how close each idea is to its first dollar.

golive._why: Once an MVP is complete (every roadmap milestone merged), a go-live build makes it launch-ready in the sandbox: SEO basics (titles, meta descriptions, share image, sitemap, robots.txt, JSON-LD), privacy and terms pages, a Buy button on STRIPE_PAYMENT_LINK, a visit beacon to RepoHQ, and a Vercel project through the credential broker. After it merges, the production URL becomes the repo homepage and the live site is audited every 6 hours (checklist step launchReady). "Get it launch-ready" on the Ideas page starts one any time after M1.

schedule._why: When the pipeline starts work by itself (lib/schedule.js; David's call on 2026-10-19: "spread out agent tasks throughout the night and day, but mostly at night"). starts: the most of each kind that may start per window (a night runs 22:00–07:00 and is named by the date it starts). auto: go-lives, first builds and the rest of started MVPs; feature: the weekly plan's features; growth: rule-based growth builds; plan: weekly plans; kit: launch kits. Quiet hours (07:00–12:00, 17:00–22:00) start nothing automatic, so David's own sessions get the Mac and the subscription. "Start build now" requests ignore it. off: true switches the windows off. 2026-10-31 (David: "tackle bigger PRs at night and really push the PC", items 1-5): first builds may start at night while the focus hold applies (build.startNew 'night'; still held in the day), and the night window allows 8 auto, 4 feature and 3 growth starts (was 6/2/2), feature.maxPerDay 6 (was 3), growth.maxBuildsPerWeek 6 (was 4). A build at the Claude usage limit pauses instead of opening a half-built PR, and automatic starts wait for the reset (lib/usage-limit.js); a build starts Docker if it's down and unloads Ollama's idle models first (lib/machine.js). The binding limit is the subscription's usage window, not the Mac: the hold makes the night use it fully without wasting runs.
